record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.original_question: Do periodic orbits in a triangular billiard correspond to scars; more precisely, are there quantum limits supported on periodic orbits?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 54 (A. Katok). Do periodic orbits in a triangular billiard correspond to scars? More precisely, are there quantum limits supported on periodic orbits?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a triangle, and consider the billiard flow on $T$: a point particle moves in straight lines inside $T$ and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) at the boundary. Consider the Laplace–Dirichlet (or Neumann) eigenvalue problem
$$-\Delta \varphi_n = \lambda_n \varphi_n \text{ in } T, \qquad \varphi_n|_{\partial T}=0,$$
with $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions $\varphi_n$ and $\lambda_n \to \infty$. A quantum limit is any weak-$*$ limit point on $T$ (or on the unit cotangent bundle, via microlocal lifts) of the sequence of probability measures $|\varphi_{n_k}(x)|^2\,dx$ along subsequences $\lambda_{n_k}\to\infty$.

A periodic orbit of the billiard flow is a closed trajectory of finite length; it gives rise to a singular invariant measure supported on the corresponding closed curve in $T$ (or on the lift of this curve in phase space). A quantum limit is said to be "scarred" on (or "supported on") a periodic orbit if its support is contained in that closed orbit (equivalently, the limit measure assigns full mass to the orbit).

Question: For a triangular billiard $T$, do there exist quantum limits whose support is contained in a periodic orbit of the billiard flow? Equivalently, do periodic orbits in triangular billiards give rise to scars in the strict sense of producing quantum limit measures supported on those orbits?
artifact.status_search_result: No definitive resolution of the question of whether quantum limits of Laplace eigenfunctions on triangular billiards can be supported on periodic orbits appears in the literature. Numerical and theoretical studies discuss scarring phenomena and candidates for scars in polygonal/triangular billiards, but a rigorous existence (or non-existence) result for quantum limits supported on periodic orbits in triangles has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Modeling Quantum Billiards with the Finite Element Method: Searching for Quantum Scarring Candidates
status_evidence.snippet: Searching for quantum scarring candidates in billiards, including triangular ones, via numerical FEM computations.
status_evidence.claim: Quantum scarring in triangular billiards remains an active area of numerical investigation rather than a settled rigorous problem.

status_evidence.title: Quantum scar - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Quantum scars are enhancements of eigenfunction density near unstable periodic orbits; rigorous results on quantum limits supported on periodic orbits are known only in special settings.
status_evidence.claim: The general question of quantum limits supported on periodic orbits in triangular billiards is not resolved.
